newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Report has little impact on Westpac bid-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Report has little impact on Westpac bid-analysts.

text.p: The planned merger between Westpac Banking Corp and Bank of Melbourne ltd will feel little impact from Wednesday's release of the Wallis report into Australia's financial system.
"It (the merger) was always going to go through," said First Pacific Stockbrokers banking analyst Andrew Turner.

"If anything there would be some very modest enhancements to the (merger) prospects but I don't believe it was required and I don't believe that the Wallis report was ever going to be the deciding factor on a Westpac-Bank of Melbourne merger," he said.

Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said he would be guided by anti-monopolies authority, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCI), in any decision on the A$1.435 billion friendly deal.
But analysts said the Treasurer's statement made little difference to the bid as the final ruling was always going to be the ACCC's call.
"I think that was always the case...I think it's always been an ACCC problem, if there is a problem," said ABN Amro analyst Michael Pulman.
